title: Wizards
subtitle: Чарівники
rules:
Deck innovationsFirst and foremost, this half-deck has a special deck with Exalted wizards: more powerful versions of the unique wizards present in the normal deck. Keep the special deck next to the market. How it works: after you have promoted one of the unique wizards, in the same turn or at any time afterwards, you can look for that wizard’s Exalted version in the special deck, and recruit them by paying the printed cost. Think of it as investing the time and resources for your wizard to study and become more powerful to work for you — now that’s what I call a job promotion! Henceforth, that Exalted wizard will sit face-up on your play area and function as a continuous sixth card for you. Each player may have only one Exalted wizard. One could even make the Exalted wizards as tiles instead of cards.Secondly, every card on this deck also has a “secondary aspect”, which is an arcane school. They activate Arcane Focus effects, kind of like in the Elemental deck, but these powers are slightly stronger because there are fewer cards for each school. However, there are 8 cards in the market deck that can activate any Arcane Focus.Finally, card #25 (Acererak the Exalted Devourer) can devour troops: send them to the devoured area.Cards v.1.1Sorted by Aspect:Obedience Cards1) Prodigious Novice Arcanist: They can activate any Arcane Focus, but only once per turn. Think of them helping the other wizards cast their spells.2) Enduring Spellbook: an alluring artifact to any wizard. The discount also works for recruiting Exalted wizards from the special deck. Or you can keep it in your deck to facilitate Arcane Focuses and cash in some VP while you’re at it.Ambition Cards3) Enchanter: enchant an enemy troop to leave its post or send it somewhere else. Also, its Focus lets you promote any card you played this turn, including itself.4) Necromancer: why keep the devoured cards out of the game?11) Ezzat: every turn you get the chance to clean your deck and pollute an opponent’s. I ran out of room on the card, but just to be clear: the card promoted face down will score negative inner-circle VP.12) Tasha the Witch: she dealt with powerful fiends from the Abyss, and they loved a sacrifice in their honor.19) Ezzat the Exalted Usurper: a bit of a shot in the dark?20) Tasha the Exalted Witch Queen: Being a powerful conjurer, Tasha can easily open portals and force enemies through. Or she can make more sacrifices to fortify fiendish friendships. About the effect: when you activate her, you take any card from the market, play it as your own once, and then promote it straight into your inner circle.Conquest Cards5) Abjurer: banish the enemies away. Also, you may manage to secure your position. You can put a point token on one of your troops just to remind everyone of that effect.9) Conjurer: literally teleport enemies or allies.13) Halaster: paranoid, crazy, powerful mage. Very destructive.14) Trobriand: more bonuses for keeping area control.21) Halaster the Exalted Mad Mage: more (seemingly) mindless destruction.22) Trobriand the Exalted Metal Mage: huge focus on the area control aspect.Guile Cards7) Diviner: planning is usually a lot easier when you can see the future... And messing with an opponent’s plans is nice as well. Also, because this is a game of intrigue and conflict, I think this card will work best if the player tells the other opponents what cards he saw, though of course that is not mandatory.8) Illusionist: agents disguised to infiltrate, gather intel and sabotage. You can even do both on the same turn if Illusion Focus activates!15) Mordenkainen: possibly sweeten your options for this turn.16) Vizeran DeVir: a simpler card, among all the crazy wizards. An austere drow.23) Mordenkainen the Exalted Planewalker: since there rarely are cards costing 2 or less, whatever comes will be a great deal.24) Vizeran DeVir the Exalted Archmage: how about an exchange they literally can’t deny? When you take the opponent’s card, bring it into your discard pile.Malice Cards9) Transmuter: simple, but thus versatile.10) Evoker: A good card for early and mid-game, but its Focus works all the way.17) Acererak: he can cast a Resurrection spell. Surely the resurrected creature will want to work for your house after such a favor.18) Muiral: as a good transmuter, he can bolster his allies.25) Acererak the Exalted Devourer: after he has killed the troops, he now consumes every speck of energy they might still have in order to feed his insatiable hunger… and you gain 2 extra VP for it!26) Muiral the Exalted Misshapen: this dude got his kicks from hunting adventurers, so you send your weaker allies as bait. You devour X cards from your hand to devour X cards from the opponents’ decks.Sorted by Arcane School:Any Arcane School:Abjuration:Conjuration:Divination:Enchantment:Evocation:Illusion:Necromancy:Transmutation:

SuggestionsA few changes may work well in getting the deck to show what it was designed to do.Katunik’s first suggestion was to replace one of the initial Nobles for a Prodigious Novice Arcanist. If there are fewer than 4 players, the remaining Arcanists go into the market deck, as per the normal game.Then, I thought about giving a secret random unique wizard to each player as the first card in their discard pile, so they could start planning purchases from round one (considering your table does not forbid perusing your own discard pile). Though this initial asymmetry may be displeasing to some players, I think it could be worth a try.Also, about the Exalted wizards, I thought of a few options for how they could work (I had the first option in mind when I wrote their effects, after all it is a race to get more powerful assets to fight for your house):• The Exalted wizard is a sixth card you can play every turn, or;• It is a sixth card option, but you can still play only five cards on your turn (maybe it will be a little more balanced, yet still powerful?), and also;• Players can have more than one Exalted Wizard in their house, but can only activate one per turn (activating more than one would surely snowball too fast).

title: Jaezred Chaulssin
subtitle: Джезред Чаульссін
rules:
SHADOWS OF THE GREAT WYRM
Faction Profile: The Jaezred Chaulssin
"The Matrons think they weave the web. They fail to realize that shadows are cast by much larger wings." — Mauzzkyl Jaezred
The Jaezred Chaulssin is a shadow-whisper in the dark—a clandestine council of shadow-dragon-blooded drow, known as the Zekyl, and their ancient Shadow Dragon progenitors. They have looked upon the spider-matriarchy of Lolth and found it wanting, choosing instead the path of calculated subversion and the cold logic of the void.
Under the iron-willed guidance of Grandfather Mauzzkyl Jaezred, the council seeks nothing less than the total collapse of the Matron Houses. They do not conquer through open war; they dismantle through political extortion, silent assassination, and the inevitable weight of long-term plots.

New Mechanic: The Ascendancy
The Jaezred Chaulssin do not merely lead; they transform. Every high-ranking member of the council exists in two states: a subtle Drow Form and an apocalyptic Dragon Form.
Only cards with the Patron Father trait may attempt this transformation. It is a permanent sacrifice of a mortal agent for ultimate draconic power.
The Trigger: When you play a Patron Father in their Drow Form, you resolve its normal effects as usual.
The Sacrifice (Promotion): After resolving the card, you may choose to Ascend. Immediately Promote the Drow card from the play area to your Inner Circle.
The Manifestation: Search the Patron Reserve for the corresponding Dragon Patron card and add it to your Discard Pile.
⚠️ Note: Ascension is a one-way path. Once a Patron Father is Promoted to summon, their Drow card remains in the Inner Circle, and the Dragon becomes your primary engine of destruction for the remainder of the game.Keep in mind that the Patron Fathers have no Inner Circle Value to reduce explosion of VP value.

Note: Ascension is an irreversible path. Once the Drow is Promoted to summon the Great Wyrm, that character's mortal form is gone, and the Dragon becomes your primary engine of destruction.

New Keyword: Draconic Vision
The Shadow Patrons possess a foresight that spans centuries. They do not react to the future; they curate it.
When a card instructs you to use Draconic Vision X:
Peer into the Void: Secretly look at the top X cards of your deck.
Claim the Future: Choose one of those cards and add it to your hand.
Burn the Rest: All remaining cards looked at are cast into your Discard Pile.

Scoring & the Inner Circle
The Zekyl and the Dragon are one soul. Therefore, they share a single space in history.
The Unique Soul: For end-game scoring, the Drow and Dragon versions of a character are treated as a Single Unique Identity.
The Finality of the Circle: You may only have one version of a character in your Inner Circle. Since the Drow form is Promoted to trigger the Ascension, the Dragon form remains in your deck.

title: The Delver’s Company
subtitle: Компанія шукачів
rules:
Tyrants of the Underdark: The Delver’s Company
Expansion Overview: The Delver’s Company is a high-stakes half-deck expansion that introduces a parallel economy. Players must balance territorial conquest with the management of their Hoard—a collection of powerful but volatile equipment and artifacts. With a d20-based Skill Check system, fortune can shift in an instant, rewarding the bold and punishing the unprepared.

I. Component Overview
40 Market Cards: Unique minions to be shuffled into the Market Deck.
30 Treasure Cards: A separate deck of items found via Skill Checks.
24 Unwanted Company Cards: "Stalker" cards that function as a more severe form of Insane Outcast.
1 Die (d20): Used for all Skill Checks.

II. The Hoard & The Appraisal Cycle
The Hoard is a personal "Relic Row" located above your player mat. It represents the physical gear your expedition is carrying.
Capacity: Your Hoard has 3 slots. If you gain a 4th Treasure, you must immediately choose one of your 4 Treasures to discard to the Treasure discard pile. You do not gain Influence for this discard.
Appraisal Timing: At the start of your turn, before playing any cards from your hand, move all Treasures currently in your Hoard to the "Appraised" status.
Selling Treasures: Appraised Treasures may be sold for their listed Influence value during your turn.
Exception: If a card says "Ignore Appraisal," you may sell a Treasure even if you acquired it during the current turn.
Hoard Immunity: Treasures in your Hoard are not considered "cards in hand" or "cards in play." They cannot be discarded or affected by opponent card effects unless a card specifically targets the Hoard.
Deck Value: All Treasures have a Deck Value of 0. They do not contribute to your final score if they are in your Hoard or discard pile at the end of the game.
Sell Value: The Promoted Value (the number in the circle usually reserved for Inner Circle VPs) on a Treasure card indicates its Sell Value in Influence.

Note on Card Formatting: > For all Treasure cards, the Promoted Value icon represents the amount of Influence gained when the card is Sold. Additionally, all Treasures have a Deck Value of 0; they provide no Victory Points during final scoring. Only Market Minions from The Delver’s Company contribute to your final VP total.

III. Treasure Activations
Treasures are single-use consumables.
The Action Limit: You are limited to 2 Treasure Activations per turn.
Activation Cost: When you activate a Treasure's ability, you resolve the effect and then discard the Treasure to the Treasure discard pile.
Bypassing the Limit: Effects that state "Activate (Ignore Limit)" do not count toward your cap of 2.
Finding & Using: You may activate a Treasure the same turn you find it, provided you have not hit your activation limit.

IV. Skill Checks2162175304800
Many minions feature a d20 icon.           When you play these cards, resolve the base effect in front of the die first, then roll for the Skill Check.
The Base Effect: You always receive the base effect of a minion (the text listed above the dice icon) regardless of your roll result.
The Critical Blunder (Natural 1): If you roll a Natural 1, the Skill Check fails regardless of any modifiers. You must immediately recruit one Unwanted Company card to your discard pile.
Modifiers: * Persistent Modifiers: (e.g., Oghma Loremaster) add to every d20 roll you make for the remainder of the turn.
Single Modifiers: (e.g., Dwarven Defender) add only to the very next Skill Check made this turn.
Rerolls: If an effect allows a reroll, the initial roll (including a Natural 1) is negated. You do not suffer the Blunder penalty if the second roll is not a 1. Take the final result as the total.

V. Unwanted Company (Stalkers)
Stalkers represent the dangers that follow an expedition home.
Placement: They are placed face-up in the Insane Outcast slot during setup.
The Tax: You cannot "play" a Stalker. To remove it, you must pay the Tax: Discard a card OR pay 2 Influence ▸ Return to supply.
Devouring/Promoting: If a Stalker would be Devoured or Promoted (by your cards or an opponent’s), it is simply returned to the supply. It provides 0 VP and cannot enter the Inner Circle.

VI. Setup & Maintenance
The Treasure Deck: Shuffle the 30 Treasures and place them face-down. Establish a discard pile next to it. When the deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile to replenish it.
Starting Treasures (Optional): Each player begins with one Drow Signet Ring in their Hoard, already Appraised.

title: Cohort
subtitle: Когорти
rules:
Introduction
Not all who support any particular drow noble house are actual members of the nobility – 
in fact, houses may have supporters who are not even drow. This mini-expansion adds some 
variation and asymmetry to the starting setup for a Tyrants of the Underdark game. 
It may also help get a player’s decks up and running faster (and perhaps a bit more evenly) 
at the start of the game.
Components
10 “Cohort” Minion cards.
Setup
Shufϐle the 10 "Cohort Minion" cards and deal two to each player, and allow each player to 
secretly select one to Recruit, discarding the other. The players reveal their selected cards 
and place that card in their discard pile like any other Recruited card.
During Play
The selected additional Minion card becomes part of a player’s deck and enters play as any 
other Recruited card as they reshufϐle. They are treated as any other card.
Variants for Setup
Once the Cohort Minion is selected and revealed, you could: 
- Place at the bottom of your draw deck.
- Devour a card of your choice in your starting deck before your initial shufϐle.
- Simply shufϐle it into your starting deck.
- Place it next to your play mat, only you can buy your selected card as if it were in the market,
then it can be purchased as any other Minion card.
